title.narrative: Child Project of the Global Clean Hydrogen Program of Malaysia

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To enhance the national institutional capacities, enabling policy frameworks, and improve technological readiness for the successful uptake of green hydrogen to ensure Malaysia meets its net zero development with social considerations and benefits.

Yes, we confirm.The Malaysia Child Project of the GCHP aims to contribute to the overall goal and impact of the programme along with the rest of the national child projects, working in a coordinated manner under the guidance of the Global Child Project. The activities envisaged for the Malaysia Child Project will support the country’s energy transition by promoting the adoption of clean hydrogen technologies while delivering wide-ranging socio-economic benefits across the target sectors.The socio-economic benefits of the Malaysia Child Project include:Capacity building and job creation:?By conducting capacity-building activities and awareness raising through national events and workshops as well as through the participation in the thematic working groups, e-training sessions, and the Global Knowledge Platform managed by the Global Child Project, stakeholders will improve their technical skills and expertise needed for the development of the clean hydrogen market. This capacity-building efforts will directly contribute to the creation of skilled jobs and improve the technical service offering in sectors linked to hydrogen production, infrastructure development, and technology management. Through the dissemination of knowledge and best practices, the project will support local industries in developing the workforce required to sustain long-term growth in the clean hydrogen economy.Innovation and industrial development:?The Malaysia Child Project will promote technological innovation by encouraging collaboration among industry stakeholders, international experts, and the local governments through the identification and support provided to the development of pilot projects using clean hydrogen. Also, by participating in the Global Knowledge Platform managed by the Global Child Project, the national projects will share best practices and innovation case studies and their experiences at local level, thus contributing to south-south cooperation and exchange, which will help spur the development of hydrogen-related technologies and industries. This will open-up new economic opportunities in industrial and transport sectors and position Malaysia and the rest of the countries as global frontrunners in the green hydrogen economy. These industries will create direct and indirect jobs, contributing to the broader socio-economic development of participating nations.Energy security and economic resilience:?Through its focus on clean hydrogen, the Malaysia Child Project will enhance energy security by supporting the development of locally produced hydrogen as a reliable alternative to imported fossil fuels. This shift will not only reduce dependency on external energy sources but will also stabilise energy prices, making the national economy more resilient to global energy market fluctuations. Increased energy independence will strengthen national energy systems, enabling countries to better meet their energy demands while ensuring a more sustainable and secure energy future.Gender inclusion and social equity:?The Malaysia Child Project will actively promote gender inclusion by ensuring that women and youth participate in all project activities. The project aims for 50% female participation and a 20% youth participation rate in project activities where applicable, thereby creating opportunities for underrepresented groups in the clean hydrogen sector. Through the development of gender-responsive knowledge products, the project will support social equity, providing equal access to new employment opportunities and ensuring that the benefits of the green hydrogen transition are widely shared across communities. Women’s voices will be systematically included in decision-making processes at the national level (e.g., validation workshops, stakeholder engagements, pilot design), and this will be tracked through gender-sensitive indicators. Furthermore, the project’s focus on skills, finance, and new industries will contribute to expanding employment opportunities for women in hydrogen-related value chains.Health and environmental benefits:?By facilitating the adoption of clean hydrogen technologies, the Malaysia Child Project will help reduce air pollution in industrial and urban areas, contributing to improved public health outcomes. Reducing reliance on fossil fuels will decrease harmful emissions, leading to better air quality and reducing health problems associated with pollution. Additionally, the environmental benefits will include the significant reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, mitigating climate change impacts and fostering healthier environments for the local population. This will also contribute to meeting national targets and commitments in terms of net-zero or low-carbon development goals.Knowledge management and sharing:?The creation of the Global Knowledge Platform by the Global Child Project and the local development of knowledge products will facilitate continuous learning, enabling Malaysia to access the latest research, best practices, and technological developments in clean hydrogen. This knowledge-sharing ecosystem will enhance the capacity of the country to innovate and implement hydrogen technologies, while also building a global community of practitioners. The socio-economic benefits of this knowledge sharing process will extend beyond the project’s lifespan, as the lessons learned and products developed will continue to be used by future generations of stakeholders, ensuring sustainable and enduring impacts both at national and international levels.
